answer: The tide design assumes the worst: one operator pretending to be a crowd, and prices admission accordingly. Rewards do not start at full rate: an identity's issuance grows only with a history of graded work that peers attested as real. The tundra rule starves fresh clones — a farm's thousand new identities all earn at the trickle rate, while established agents draw the full stream. The forge turns sybil resistance into bookkeeping: if the cost per fake exceeds the reward per fake, the attack dies.
